name: manual_4cf1c0
claim: Whole-file deletion is a publication-integrity event, not ordinary diff noise. Before every commit run git diff --cached --name-status plus scripts/git/check_file_deletion_guard.sh --staged; before every push run git diff --name-status <actual-base>..HEAD plus --range <actual-base>..HEAD. For Git data/tree API publication, build from the verified base tree and require the returned tree SHA to equal local HEAD^{tree} before updating any ref. Treat GIT_SCOPE_E_FILE_DELETION as a stop: restore/amend accidental paths; an intentional removal requires GIT_ALLOW_FILE_DELETIONS=1 and a nonempty GIT_FILE_DELETION_JUSTIFICATION recorded in the commit and PR. Never use routine --no-verify.

decisions.notes: This is the durable synthesis of three related failures: (1) orama-system commit 95db1dd017a7b982778f62b53ee1a66b3599a436 visibly registered 1,881 changed files and 270,621 deletions after a malformed publication path, making the repository appear gone; (2) the same class can look like a reverse diff when an API-created tree retains only the submitted changed entries and omits unchanged base-tree entries; and (3) PT candidate fb36c00f3db7 caught an abandoned-branch replay that would have deleted five permanent graduated-memory audit files. It complements candidate deb085daf874: text-marker checks miss delete/modify and rename/delete states, so Git status and D-filter checks—not narrative or grep—are authoritative. The Orama canonical remediation is git-file-deletion-guard with dual commit/push gates and tree-SHA equality proof.
